story_ai.headline: GIFT Nifty hints at 150‑point gap‑up as global cues turn mixed
paragraphs: GIFT Nifty is at 22837.5, down 29 points (-0.13%). The implied open gap of about 149.85 points (0.66%) above yesterday’s close of 22687.7 suggests a gap‑up start for the Indian market.

Overnight, US equity indices closed lower – S&P 500 at 7663.4 (-1.21%), Nasdaq at 26008.9 (-2.60%) and Dow at 52868.0 (+0.02%). US futures now show a modest dip in the S&P 500 (-0.01%) but a small rise in Nasdaq (+0.17%) and a dip in Dow (-0.16%). In Asia, Nikkei fell to 61825.3 (-1.72%) and Kospi to 5409.7 (-2.24%) while Hang Seng edged up to 22956.7 (+0.10%) and Shanghai slipped to 3607.5 (-1.38%). Europe ended softer with FTSE 100 at 10725.0 (-0.26%) and DAX at 25371.8 (-1.07%).

Commodities show mixed signals – Brent crude at $113.93 (+0.67%) and WTI at $100.21 (+0.74%) keep energy costs elevated, while gold slipped to $4030.7 (-0.73%) and silver to $54.2 (-1.48%). Copper rose modestly to $6.42 (+0.34%) and natural gas fell to $2.8 (-1.14%). The rupee held steady at Rs 94.81 per dollar, the dollar index nudged up to 101.7 (+0.07%) and the US 10‑year yield eased to 4.95% (down 19 bps). Higher oil prices could pressure input costs, but a stable rupee and lower US yields may ease funding pressures for Indian issuers.

Foreign Institutional Investors have sold Rs 7704 crore over the past five days, while Domestic Institutional Investors bought Rs 7365 crore. Nifty options show a PCR of 0.82, max‑pain at 22850, a call wall at 24000 and a put wall at 22000 – historically sensitive levels that could guide price action today.

Earnings season is in full swing with results from ADANIPOWER, INFY, JSWSTEEL, BPCL and many others slated for release. US data – Flash Manufacturing PMI and Flash Services PMI at 19:15, followed by Revised UoM Consumer Sentiment and Inflation Expectations at 19:30 – will add to market tone. A Nasdaq decline of 2.60% is flagged as a bearish cue for Indian IT stocks.

Key headlines: NLC India signed an MoU for a 3200 MW ultra‑supercritical coal plant, boosting the Power and Coal sectors; GIFT Nifty’s gap‑up hint points to a broadly positive opening; Brent crude crossing $113 adds pressure on Energy stocks; the Nasdaq weakness may weigh on Indian IT; overall market sentiment remains mixed but historically sensitive to these cues.
